Fiberglass vs concrete vs vinyl: which suits Florida?

Install time, upkeep, feel underfoot and lifetime cost, compared honestly.

6 min readBy the iTop Pools crewUpdated November 2026
Key takeaways
  • Fiberglass is typically installed in 2–6 weeks, concrete in 3–6 months.
  • Fiberglass has a smooth, non-porous surface and rarely carries a big future cost.
  • Choose concrete for a truly custom shape, and vinyl for the lowest upfront price.

Almost every Jacksonville buyer starts with the same question: which type of pool? All three can be great. They just suit different priorities.

How do fiberglass, concrete and vinyl compare?

CompareFiberglassConcreteVinyl liner
Typical install2–6 weeks3–6 monthsSeveral weeks
SurfaceSmooth gelcoatPlaster or pebble, texturedSoft vinyl
Shape freedomChoose from moldsAny shapeMany shapes
Big future costRareResurfacingLiner replacement

Why is fiberglass popular in Florida?

A fiberglass shell is made in a factory and set in one piece, so the build is short and less weather-dependent. That matters in a Florida summer. The gelcoat surface is smooth and non-porous, which gives algae less to grip. Barrier Reef estimates vinyl pools use about 50% more chemicals than fiberglass.

When does concrete make sense?

If you want a vanishing edge, an unusual size or a shape no mold offers, concrete (gunite) is the answer. Expect a longer build and periodic resurfacing over the pool's life.

Where does vinyl fit?

Vinyl usually has the lowest upfront price. Barrier Reef puts fiberglass at roughly 15–20% more than vinyl. The liner wears and needs replacing, which industry guides put at around every 10 years.

Our take: for most Northeast Florida families who want to swim this season and spend weekends swimming rather than scrubbing, fiberglass is the best balance. If your yard needs something truly custom, we'll tell you.

Sources: Barrier Reef Pools USA FAQ (install time, chemical use, price vs vinyl); published industry comparison guides (concrete build time, liner life).
